cosy-lesson.title: My Life With & My Life Without AI (B1)

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Automation ≠ manual labor – the use of automatic equipment in a process.

p.em: Example: AI automation speeds up administrative paperwork.

cosy-blockquote.p: Efficiency ≠ delay – the state or quality of being efficient.

p.em: Example: Using AI tools increases daily work efficiency.

cosy-blockquote.p: Creativity ≠ routine – the use of imagination or original ideas.

p.em: Example: Relying on AI summaries can limit human creativity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dependency ≠ self-reliance – the state of relying on someone or something for support.

p.em: Example: Overusing search assistants creates digital dependency.

cosy-blockquote.p: Outsource ≠ perform – to obtain goods or services from an outside supplier.

p.em: Example: We should not outsource critical thinking to machines.

cosy-blockquote.p: Algorithm ≠ human thought – a process or set of rules followed by a computer.

p.em: Example: Recommender algorithms shape our online habits.

cosy-blockquote.p: Originality ≠ imitation – the ability to think independently and creatively.

p.em: Example: Originality remains a uniquely human characteristic.

cosy-blockquote.p: Productivity ≠ stagnation – the effectiveness of productive effort.

p.em: Example: AI assistants boost student writing productivity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive ≠ physical – relating to mental processes of knowledge and memory.

p.em: Example: Mental math exercises protect our cognitive agility.

cosy-blockquote.p: Unplug ≠ connect – to disconnect an electrical device or take a screen break.

p.em: Example: Taking time to unplug restores mental focus.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How has workplace automation changed daily task routines in modern offices?
★ Which routine task in your job would you love to automate?

In what ways does using generative AI improve personal writing efficiency?
★ Do you use AI assistants like ChatGPT for drafting emails?

Can AI tools enhance human creativity or do they replace artistic originality?
★ Have you used AI tools to generate images or digital art?

Why are some professionals worried about growing technological dependency on AI?
★ How reliant are you on smartphone apps for daily tasks?

What types of complex analysis can companies safely outsource to intelligent algorithms?
★ Would you trust an AI algorithm to manage your personal finances?

How does a machine learning algorithm personalize your social media news feed?
★ Do you feel your online feeds accurately reflect your interests?

What defines true human originality in literature and visual arts?
★ Can an AI-created song ever have genuine soul?

How does adopting digital AI tools boost overall business productivity?
★ Has AI made you faster at finishing daily work?

What is the difference between human cognitive reasoning and algorithmic pattern recognition?
★ Are you fascinated by artificial intelligence progress?

Why is it important to periodically unplug from digital devices and AI tools?
★ How often do you spend a full day completely offline?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Widespread automation will create more new job opportunities than it destroys. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Are you optimistic or concerned about AI in the job market?

Using AI tools to maximize personal work efficiency will become mandatory for all professionals. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you actively learn new AI tools?

True artistic creativity can only originate from human emotional experience. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Can AI art ever match human masterpieces?

Over-reliance on AI will cause psychological dependency and diminish human critical thinking. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Worried about future generations losing basic skills?

It is safe to outsource routine administrative decisions to automated algorithms. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Trust automated hiring or loan application screening?

Every social media algorithm should be audited by independent ethics boards. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Support government regulation of algorithms?

AI-generated content lacks genuine emotional originality and cultural depth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Can you tell the difference between human and AI writing?

Integrating AI into daily workflows raises overall national productivity significantly. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Has tech improved your work-life balance?

Human cognitive flexibility will always stay superior to artificial intelligence systems. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Believe Artificial General Intelligence will happen soon?

Learning to unplug regularly is necessary to maintain mental health in the digital age. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you protect your offline personal time?

ul.li: Incorrect: AI makes me to work faster. → Correct: AI makes me work faster. ((Causative verb 'make' takes a bare infinitive: 'make me work'.))
Incorrect: I rely in AI tools. → Correct: I rely on AI tools. ((Preposition rule: 'rely' collocates with 'on'.))
